doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Playing styles, cruises and tribute bands
title: Darius Brubeck and the Brubeck sons
summary: He played with Darius Brubeck on trombone, comments on the pressure of a famous father, and mentions Danny and Paul Desmond's saxophone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Darius Brubeck? You played with him and everywhere from there to the Coasters.

Yes. Like I say I am versatile and jazz is my music but I bring something from all these experiences into my playing. I was doing a big band show with what I’ll call a vintage big band, it was playing a concert. And I looked to my left and there was Darius Brubeck playing trombone. And an excellent musician. And again he was coming out of his jazz context into the vintage music style to add something to his jazz repertoire. And an excellent musician, and I envy people that can jump from trombone and play bass as well. It’s having a father like Dave Brubeck, it’s tough. Because you’re out there and © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
people automatically expect you to be great. And it’s something you have to deal with when your spouse is a musician.
His other son is quite a good drummer.

Danny, yeah, excellent. They’re all fine musicians and something that I found out — that when Paul Desmond passed away he left his saxophone to the Brubeck son who did not choose to play music, in hopes that someday he would pick up the saxophone, which I thought was very interesting.
